posts.text: SEBI’s CAS consultation gets 20,000 responses — image 598×246 33.3 KB Source : moneycontrol SEBI has received around 20,000 comments on its consultation paper around the Closing Auction Session (CAS), market timings and derivative settlement methodology. That’s quite a jump from the roughly 3,500 responses reported a few days ago. It’s also more than three times the 6,000 responses SEBI received in 2024 on its consultation around curbing excessive F&O activity. posts.author: Kabir_B
posts.text: Stock futures prices also not aligned after CAS — If ABB has closed at ₹6,660 through CAS and someone is still willing to buy the future at ₹6,980 till 3:40, there has to be some reason for that bid. The thing is once CAS is over, you can’t go and buy ABB at ₹6,660 anymore. So the normal cash-futures arbitrage isn’t really available after the price is known. Maybe that’s why SEBI is already looking at this exact issue and has proposed either a blended CTS + CAS VWAP or, as an interim option, going back to CTS VWAP for expiry settlement. posts.author: Patel_6
posts.text: Stock futures prices also not aligned after CAS — I think the situation in Union Bank and ABB is normal, bcz the CAS closing price may not necessarily the “true” closing price. In both cases, the bid/ask levels in the market depth were broadly around the reference price. For 174 bid in Union Bank ,there could be several reasons for such an order for example, someone who had shorted fut and don’t want to get into the physical delivery, or someone trying to square off/net a position related to options.

posts.author: Rohith_Raj
posts.text: Stock futures prices also not aligned after CAS — Really interesting observation. I also feel CAS has created a genuine disconnect between the cash and F&O markets, especially in those last few minutes. The kind of price gaps you’ve pointed out can definitely make convergence and settlement more complicated. This is something most of us may not notice unless we actually track the prices closely. NSE should look at synchronising the closing timings of cash and F&O, or at least review how the final settlement price is arrived at.
